issues.body: check_instrument() sums cache_writes but never rejects a nonzero value. That violates the load-bearing claim that measure trials are read-only and independent: if READ_ONLY is misspelled, unsupported, or otherwise ineffective, earlier concurrent/sequential trials can populate the namespace and bias later trials. The self-test hides this gap by giving every nominal treatment record cache_writes=260, so the supposedly valid ADOPT and DO-NOT-ADOPT cases explicitly demonstrate that a writing treatment still receives a verdict.
issues.fix_hint: Require treatment cache_writes == 0 before rendering either verdict and return INCONCLUSIVE otherwise. Change _rec()'s valid default to cache_writes=0 and add a mutation case with nonzero writes that must exit 2.
issues.title: Treatment cache writes do not make the experiment inconclusive

issues.body: --bar-seconds accepts any float without validation. A dispatch with 0 or a negative value can emit ADOPT for no improvement (or a regression), while NaN emits a confident DO-NOT-ADOPT because every comparison with NaN is false. This contradicts the documented policy that the 60-second bar cannot be lowered to fit a result and makes the workflow input a route to an invalid terminal verdict.
issues.fix_hint: Validate that the bar is finite and at least DEFAULT_BAR_SECONDS, failing without a verdict otherwise; alternatively remove the workflow input if rescoring below the precommitted threshold is not a supported operation. Add self-tests for zero, negative, below-default, NaN, and infinity.
issues.title: The precommitted 60-second adoption bar is not enforced

verdict.summary: The harness is thoughtfully fail-closed for several failure modes, but it can still issue a confident verdict when the treatment trials wrote to the shared sccache namespace, invalidating the claimed independence of the five samples. The implementation also accepts arbitrary and non-finite adoption bars despite documenting 60 seconds as a precommitted policy threshold. Both defects affect the trustworthiness of the experiment's terminal verdict.
